As vibecoding becomes increasingly popular, the number of newly listed apps on the App Store has surged, doubling in the first half of 2026, but downloads have only grown by 2%. Details below.

New listings surge, but downloads lag far behind

The New York Times published a report today, citing Sensor Tower data showing that although the number of newly listed apps on the App Store doubled in the first half of 2026, downloads only increased by 2%:

The New York Times report also interviewed two developers who have been releasing vibecoding apps on the App Store: Marco Pérez plans to leave his job at JPMorgan next month to work on app development full-time; David Svensson has launched 11 niche apps in the past five months and views vibecoding more as a hobby than a business opportunity.

The report is as follows:

Pérez, a software engineer based in Chicago who had never developed a mobile app before, spent five weeks over the winter experimenting with "vibecoding" AI tools to build a prototype, then spent two more weeks preparing it for release on the App Store. The app, called InfoDrizzle, has performed reasonably well, recording 1,300 downloads to date and earning roughly US$500 in profit. Pérez's next app has proven even more popular. In May this year, he spent only about a week launching Stampa — a scrapbooking app that turns photos into digital postage stamps. Stampa has been downloaded 20,000 times and earned about US$3,000 in profit.

Apple spokesperson Peter Ajemian addressed another impact of the surge in submissions when responding to The New York Times: earlier reports indicated that the App Store review process was under significant pressure.

Ajemian said: "Apple has consistently been able to review 90% of app submissions within 48 hours", and added that Apple is "delighted that a new generation of developers is using the latest tools to build and release apps at the fastest pace in history".

He also noted that regardless of whether an app is developed through vibecoding, "all apps must meet the same rigorous quality, privacy, and security standards that users have always trusted".
